sections.title: The Altar of Incense
observations: In this section, God instructs Moses to build an altar for burning incense, which is to be placed in front of the veil that separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place. This altar symbolizes the prayers of the people ascending to God, emphasizing the importance of prayer in worship.

The specific materials and dimensions of the altar are given, highlighting the care and precision required in the construction of items used in the worship of God. This reflects the holiness of God and the need for His people to approach Him with reverence.

sections.title: The Atonement Money
observations: God commands the Israelites to give a half shekel as atonement money when they are counted. This practice serves as a reminder of their need for atonement and the cost of sin.
The atonement money is used for the service of the tabernacle, illustrating the communal responsibility of the Israelites in supporting the worship of God.

sections.title: The Bronze Basin
observations: The bronze basin is to be made for the priests to wash their hands and feet before entering the tabernacle. This act of washing symbolizes the need for purity and holiness before approaching God.
The instructions emphasize that the priests must wash to avoid death, underscoring the seriousness of approaching God without proper preparation.

sections.title: The Anointing Oil and Incense
observations: God provides a recipe for the anointing oil and the incense, which are to be used exclusively for sacred purposes. This highlights the importance of setting apart certain items and practices for God’s service.
The prohibition against using the anointing oil and incense for personal use underscores the sanctity of what is dedicated to God.

importantVerses.commentary: The altar of incense is placed before the mercy seat, emphasizing the connection between prayer and God's mercy.
The atonement money serves as a reminder of the cost of sin and the need for redemption.
The requirement for priests to wash before entering the tabernacle highlights the necessity of spiritual cleanliness.

questions: What does the altar of incense teach us about the nature of prayer and worship?
How does the concept of atonement money relate to our understanding of redemption in Christ?
In what ways can we apply the principle of spiritual cleanliness in our own lives today?
